title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from pp. 77-80. X is a variety, in practice a curve, over a field K finitely generated over Q, with Galois group Γ = Gal(K̄/K). The points x, y are K-rational, and Π̂1(X) is the profinite étale fundamental groupoid of X_K̄. Since x and y are rational, Γ acts on the set of étale paths π̂1(X; x, y). That set is a bitorsor under (π̂1(X,y), π̂1(X,x)): π̂1(X,y) acts on the left, π̂1(X,x) on the right, and the Γ-action is compatible with both.

For a path ℓ : x → y, p. 78 defines two 1-cocycles:
- f_ℓ(u) = ℓ^{-1}·^uℓ ∈ π̂1(X,x);
- g_ℓ(u) = ^uℓ·ℓ^{-1} ∈ π̂1(X,y).
Changing ℓ (formula (31)) changes each cocycle only within its cohomology class. So one gets nonabelian classes f_{y,x} ∈ H^1(Γ, π̂1(X,x)) and g_{y,x} ∈ H^1(Γ, π̂1(X,y)). Each is the class of the Γ-equivariant path torsor, and they correspond under the canonical outer isomorphism π̂1(X,x) ≅ π̂1(X,y).

This page adds three things.
(i) Everything can be phrased intrinsically through the Γ-equivariant bitorsor π̂1(X; x, y).
(ii) f and g determine each other, and both are determined by a single cocycle f_ℓ or g_ℓ, as in (33). The margin formula (34) makes this explicit for the inverse path: g_{ℓ^{-1}}(u) = f_ℓ(u)^{-1} and f_{ℓ^{-1}}(u) = g_ℓ(u)^{-1}.
(iii) A remark on a simply connected 'T^α' inside X containing x and y. Most plausibly this is a 1-connected region giving a privileged path class, perhaps a tangential or tree-like base. In that case the cocycles are determined by the restricted datum 𝔗^{T^α}_{x,y}. The reading is uncertain.

Grothendieck then states that if X embeds in an abelian variety, or more generally in a semi-abelian variety (an extension of an abelian variety by a torus), Mordell-Weil gives injectivity. For fixed x0, the point x is determined by the class f_{x0,x}, and in fact by one cocycle f_ℓ. He contrasts this with the case where x0 varies.

The argument intended is the standard one. Push forward to the generalized Jacobian or semi-abelian variety A, and use the abelian Kummer map. A(K) → H^1(Γ, T̂A) is injective because A(K) is finitely generated (Mordell-Weil, with Lang-Néron for function fields over Q), so ∩_n nA(K) = 0. This is the injectivity half of what became the section conjecture, i.e. the nonabelian Kummer map X(K) → H^1(Γ, π̂1(X_K̄, x0)).

The next page goes on to the 'very interesting and surely deep' problem of explicitly determining f_ℓ. There u ∈ Γ is to be coordinatized by the values f_{ℓ_j}(u) on generators ℓ_j of a groupoid Π1(X, I) with several base points.
errors: (33) writes g_ℓ : Γ → π̂1(Y,y); this should be π̂1(X,y). It is a slip, copied from the 'π̂1(Y,y)' of the outer isomorphism on p. 78.
Index conventions are inconsistent: f_{x,y} versus f_{y,x}, and g_{y,x} versus g_{x,y}, are used interchangeably between pages.

Formula (34) checks out with the conventions f_a(u) = a^{-1}·^u a and g_b(u) = ^u b·b^{-1}. With ℓ : x → y, both g_{ℓ^{-1}}(u) = ^u(ℓ^{-1})·ℓ and f_ℓ(u)^{-1} = (ℓ^{-1}·^uℓ)^{-1} are loops at x and are equal.

The Mordell-Weil injectivity claim is only sketched. It needs X(K) → A(K) to be injective (e.g. Albanese or generalized Jacobian embedding of a curve with a rational point). The phrase about x0 varying ('bidon') is left unclear.

ideas.what: Galois-equivariant bitorsor of étale paths between rational points, and the associated nonabelian 1-cocycles f_ℓ, g_ℓ with classes in H^1(Γ, π̂1(X,x)).
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian Kummer map / path torsor class (section map X(K) → H^1(Γ, π1))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); later Deligne (1989), Wojtkowiak, Kim (2005, unipotent version)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27 June 1983), circulated and published in Geometric Galois Actions I (1997); Esquisse d'un programme alludes to it

ideas.what: Formulas relating the left and right cocycles and inverse paths: g_{ℓ^{-1}} = f_ℓ^{-1} and f_{ℓ^{-1}} = g_ℓ^{-1}.
Injectivity of x ↦ class of the path torsor, via Mordell-Weil, for X embedded in an abelian or semi-abelian variety.
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of the section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1983 letter); written proofs by Nakamura, Mochizuki, Stix and others

ideas.what: Cocycles determined by data on a simply connected 'T^α' ⊂ X containing x, y, i.e. a privileged path class (reading uncertain).
ideas.modern_name: Canonical paths / tangential base points (Deligne 1989, Ihara)

missed.claim: This page is an early, explicitly worked-out version of the nonabelian Kummer map using left/right bitorsor cocycles. It also flags (continued on p. 80) the program of explicitly computing f_ℓ by coordinatizing Γ through its action on paths between several rational base points. That foreshadows Wojtkowiak's Galois polylogarithms and Kim's nonabelian Chabauty, but the later literature reached these independently. This is a historical precedence detail, not a new result.
missed.quote: f_{x,y} et g_{y,x} se déterminent mutuellement, et qu'ils sont déterminés par la connaissance d'un seul f_ℓ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's pre-1983 formulation of the path-torsor / Kummer map viewpoint in the multi-base-point groupoid form now used in Kim's and Wojtkowiak's work.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is the standard nonabelian Kummer map and the Mordell-Weil injectivity argument, both known from Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings. The only mild interest is the bitorsor and multi-base-point formulation and the obscure T^α remark.
transcription_corrections: (33): the image indeed reads 'π̂1(Y,y)', a slip for π̂1(X,y); the side note reads 'ℓ : x → y (dans Π1(X))'.
Margin NB: reads roughly 'f_{x,y} et f_{y,x} (ou g_{x,y} et g_{y,x}) se déterminent mutuellement, et en termes de ℓ ... (34) g_{ℓ^{-1}}(u) = f_ℓ(u)^{-1}, f_{ℓ^{-1}}(u) = g_ℓ(u)^{-1}'.
'(p. ex. "semi-abéliennes")' is more likely '(p. ex. X courbe alg. "...")', with the quoted adjective unclear.
Line 3: 'et l'opération de Γ sur [-tout-] ça fonctoriellement' plausibly reads 'sur tout ça, fonctoriellement'.
'pour un x0 fixé ... (mais si x0 varie ... bidon !)': the image shows 'x_n' written above x0, perhaps indicating varying base points.
